protein kinases are essential in the regulation of proteins involved in MDR, that protein kinase inhibitors may be able to modulate MDR, and that protein kinase inhibitors can enhance the activity of antitumor drugs.
the expression of several proteins involved at the development of antineoplastic drug resistance is regulated via protein phosphorylation.

(i) ras-induced Fos expression is under positive regulation of PKC; (ii) the expression of the mdr-3-encoded P-glyco protein is also under PKC-dependent regulation; (iii) the expression of GST is under positive regulation by ras, and (iv) the cytotoxicity enhancement by protein kinase C (ilofosine) of the antitumor drug ds-platinum is probably caused by a reduction of PK-dependent Fos expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein phosphorylation in the development of drug resistance and its potential as target for the modulation of MDR.
the role of protein kinases, in particular PKC, CKII, and ras, in the development of MDR.
the role of protein phosphorylation and the regulation of protein kinases as potential tools for the modulation of MDR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein kinases are involved in the development and expression of drug resistance, and that they can be used as targets to reduce the development of drug resistance.
the activity of several proteins which determine the development of antineoplastic drug resistance is regulated via protein phosphorylation.

protein kinase inhibitors are able to modulate the expression of proteins which are involved in the development or maintenance of MDR and that they can synergistically enhance the antitumor activity of several drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of proteins which are essential for the development of drug resistance is under the control of protein kinases.
PKC inhibitors are useful tools in the development of new drugs against cancer.
protein phosphorylation is an important mechanism of regulation of the expression of proteins which are essential for antitumor drug sensitivity.

PKC inhibitors may be useful for reducing drug resistance and enhancing the efficacy of antitumor agents.
protein kinases are potentially useful targets to reduce the expression of proteins which are essential for the development of drug resistance.
